Accessibility First

Accessibility isn't an afterthought—it's built into every component, pattern, and workflow from day one.

WCAG 2.2 Design Goals

Accessibility work focuses on color contrast, visible focus indicators, and semantic markup, using WCAG 2.2 AA as a reference. Compliance requires testing of each complete implementation.

4.5:1
Min Contrast
Review
Keyboard navigation

Screen Reader Support

ARIA labels, live regions, semantic HTML, and mathematical rendering support are used to improve access. Screen-reader behavior needs verification in the target application.

Review
ARIA Labels
AA
Design target

Focus Management

Visible focus states, logical tab order, and keyboard shortcuts throughout all interactive elements. Skip links and landmarks for efficient navigation.

Systems Thinker. Accessibility Advocate. EdTech Founder.

I design and build scalable systems that make education technology more accessible, efficient, and delightful for educators and students alike. As founder of Item Orchard LLC, I've created AI-powered knowledge graphs, standards mapping tools, and dynamic assessment platforms for K-12 content and assessment workflows.

My flagship products—OrchardGraphX (curriculum intelligence platform), OrchardLearnX (content analysis & customization), OrchardTranslate (multilingual content accessibility), and OrchardView (PDF-to-knowledge-graph processing)—explore ways to visualize learning progressions and support content development and review.

I believe great design systems aren't just about consistency—they're about enabling teams to move faster while maintaining quality and accessibility standards. Every interface I build prioritizes educator time constraints and student accessibility needs.
